mechanics.normalEncounterPercentMeaning: Share of successful unboosted encounters in this habitat.
mechanics.futureTeamLevelOneRule: A normal spawn whose listed minimum level is above 1 has this independent chance to appear at level 1.
mechanics.honeyRule: Honey replaces the normal pool with the two rarest distinct species in that habitat.

honeyPoolShares.note: Unboosted shares from the server honey weights. Active world boosts may alter unlikely encounter odds.

mechanics.fishingRule: Fishing is a separate method: with a Fishing Rod, face a fishable water tile and cast. About 78% of casts hook something. Maps without a dedicated water habitat use the shared Karel default rod pool; water habitats reuse their own encounter pool.
mechanics.shinyRule: Shiny odds and active server boosts are intentionally displayed live in game rather than frozen into this guide.
mechanics.celebrationRule: Staff-scheduled Alpha Celebration swarms are dynamic and appear in game while active; they are not fixed route spawns.

habitats.title: Lupies abandoned / Lupies School Secret S.4
Ocana Mine A / Ocana Mine B

fishing.requirement: An Old, Good, or Super Rod and a fishable water tile: face open water and cast. The rod tier gates what you can hook — the Old Rod reaches common/uncommon water Pokemon, the Good Rod adds Rare and Super Rare, and the Super Rod adds Mega and Ultra Rare.

defaultRodPool.title: Karel Default Rod Pool
defaultRodPool.appliesTo: Casting on open water on any Alpha map whose encounter habitat is not itself a water habitat.

localWaterPools.title: Ocana Mine C
localWaterPools.note: Reused as a rod pool only because its habitat label matches the fishing water pattern; its roster holds no Water-type species. This mirrors the current rollFishingEncounter behavior and should be confirmed by the gameplay owner.

localWaterPools.title: Sea Cave / Cave Shuckle
localWaterPools.note: Casting on water here draws from this habitat's own encounter pool (listed above), not the default rod pool.
